messages.subject: Running sem with a factor
parts:
Dear Group,
I have run the following code and obtained an error. 

I previously ran the model using lavaan without the additional regression in the final line of the specification of cfa3.model.375 and without the 'ordered' keyword in the call to lavaan, obtaining expected results. Without the additional regression, I was confirming the roles of three factors in explaining my data.

However then I added the regression for the variable 'Q4.Attended.Beltane.before'. This variable is numeric and consists entirely of ones or zeroes. It seemed from reading the lavaan documentation that adding 'ordered = Q4.Attended.Beltane.before' to the lavaan call was sufficient for the regression.  But, I get the error message show at the bottom of this post.

Can anybody help, please?

Russ

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: RE: Running sem with a factor
parts:
Russell-

     First, make sure that the distribution of the 0-1 variable includes both 0s and 1s.  The message indicates that there is only one value among the 79 cases.

     Second, the regression you propose should be estimated using a logistic regression, and lavaan does not encompass logistic regression.  The closest you might come is to define a common factor, then specify this observed variable as the sole indicator of that common factor and “ordered,” and then use the factor as outcome variable in your regression.

--Ed Rigdon

Thanks Ed,
Your suggestion of defining a common factor worked.  Thank you very much.

However, I am still perplexed by the original specification not working.  In deciding to try that I (thought) I was following instructions on http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html as per the second choice:

Endogenous categorical variables

The lavaan 0.5 series can deal with binary and ordinal (but not nominal) endogenous variables. Only the three-stage WLS approach is currently supported, including some 'robust' variants. To use binary/ordinal data, you have two choices:

  1. declare them as 'ordered' (using the ordered function, which is part of base R) in your data.frame before you run the analysis; for example, if you need to declare four variables (say, item1, item2, item3, item4) as ordinal in your data.frame (called Data), you can use something like:

    Data[,c("item1",
        "item2",
        "item3",
        "item4")] <-
    lapply(Data[,c("item1",
                   "item2",
                   "item3",
                   "item4")], ordered)

  2. use the ordered argument when using one of the fitting functions (cfa/sem/growth/lavaan), for example, if you have four binary or ordinal variables (say, item1, item2, item3, item4), you can use:

    fit <- cfa(myModel, data = myData,
           ordered=c("item1","item2",
                     "item3","item4"))

In both cases, lavaan will automatically switch to the WLSMV estimator: it will use diagonally weighted least squares (DWLS) to estimate the model parameters, but it will use the full weight matrix to compute robust standard errors, and a mean- and variance-adjusted test stastistic.

Any illumination on what I have done incorrectly would be very helpful.


Again thanks very much,

Russ

messages.subject: RE: Running sem with a factor
parts:
Russell—

     In the writing that you cite, I think that the status of these variables as indicators of a factor was assumed.  Remember, we can estimate a structural equation model from only a covariance or correlation matrix and a suitable weight matrix.  WLSMV is an approach for dealing with that kind of problem.  By treating the observed variable as an indicator of a factor, you have specified your model in a way that allows that machinery to work.  But no, I don’t know exactly why lavaan was giving you that particular error message.

--Ed Rigdon

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Running sem with a factor
parts:
On 01/07/2015 01:11 PM, Russell Rimmer wrote:
> However then I added the regression for the variable
> 'Q4.Attended.Beltane.before'. This variable is numeric and consists
> entirely of ones or zeroes. It seemed from reading the lavaan
> documentation that adding 'ordered = Q4.Attended.Beltane.before' to the
> lavaan call was sufficient for the regression. But, I get the error
> message show at the bottom of this post.

You are using the lavaan() function, and that is driving without a seatbelt!

What happens if you use the sem() function instead? If you must use the
lavaan() function, you should keep in mind that:

- when you add the 'ordered' argument, you are switching to
'categorical' model, and this implies meanstructure = TRUE; but by
default, all the intercepts will be fixed to zero, so you need to free
them up

- you need to provide parameter(s) for the threshold(s) of all
categorical variables (in your case: Q4.Attended.Beltane.before)

Compare this:

library(lavaan)
HS.model <- ' visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9

y ~ visual + textual + speed
'

Data <- HolzingerSwineford1939
Data$y <- c(rep(1,200), rep(0,101))

fit <- sem(HS.model, data = Data, ordered = "y", std.lv = TRUE)

versus


HS.model <- ' visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9

# factor variances + covariances
visual ~~ 1*visual
textual ~~ 1*textual
speed ~~ 1*speed
visual ~~ textual + speed
textual ~~ speed

# residual variances indicators
x1 ~~ x1; x2 ~~ x2; x3 ~~ x3
x4 ~~ x4; x5 ~~ x5; x6 ~~ x6
x7 ~~ x7; x8 ~~ x8; x9 ~~ x9

y ~ visual + textual + speed
'

fit <- lavaan(HS.model, data = Data, ordered = "y")

The latter will fail. But this should work:

fit <- lavaan(HS.model, data = Data, ordered = "y", auto.th = TRUE,
int.ov.free = TRUE)

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Running sem with a factor
parts:
On 01/07/2015 02:08 PM, Edward Rigdon wrote:
> Second, the regression you propose should be estimated using a
> logistic regression, and lavaan does not encompass logistic regression.
> The closest you might come is to define a common factor, then specify
> this observed variable as the sole indicator of that common factor and
> “ordered,” and then use the factor as outcome variable in your regression.

It is true that lavaan (0.5-17) does not do logistic regression, but it
does probit regression instead. No need to construct phantom factors.

Yves.
